title: Summer squash, yellow or green, frozen, cooked with oil

content.title: About
content.content: Summer squash (zucchini) is an annual plant of the Cucurbitaceae family grown for its edible fruits. The frozen product consists of pre‑sliced yellow or green pieces that are flash‑frozen to retain most of their flavor and nutrients. When cooked with a little oil they become tender and aromatic.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Summer squash belongs to the same family as pumpkin, melon and watermelon.
Yellow varieties get their color from the natural pigment xanthophyll.
Freezing is done within 30–45 minutes after harvest, minimizing vitamin loss.
A quick sauté in a small amount of oil keeps the squash slightly crisp.
In many cuisines it is used in stews, soups and casseroles.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect the eyes from age‑related changes.

items.title: Provides beta‑carotene (vitamin A)
items.content: Beta‑carotene is important for vision and skin health.

items.title: Cucurbit allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to summer squash.

items.title: Sodium content in processed product
items.content: If the frozen squash is salted, consider the total sodium intake in the diet.

items.title: Possible pesticide residues
items.content: When buying frozen vegetables, choose reputable brands that test for residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sauté the frozen squash pieces in a skillet with a little oil for 5–7 minutes until tender and lightly golden. Add them to pasta, rice, omelets, soups, or serve as a side dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen squash in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After thawing, use within 1–2 days and do not refreeze.
